editorial:
The Kid is a 1921 American silent comedy-drama written, directed by and starring Charlie Chaplin. First National Pictures distributed it. It was the first feature Chaplin directed, and it follows the Tramp as he raises an abandoned boy played by Jackie Coogan. The Library of Congress selected it for the National Film Registry in December 2011.

The 1921 print is in the US public domain because its term has expired. The rights trap is the music. Chaplin later removed scenes he thought too sentimental and composed and recorded a new score for a re-edited reissue, which premiered in 1972. That version and its score are not covered by the 1921 expiry. A 2016 score by Craig Safan is separate again. Use a copy of the 1921 cut with no score, or with music you have cleared.
faq: Can I reuse footage from The Kid (1921) in my own video?
Yes for the 1921 images. The print's US copyright term has expired. Use the 1921 cut, not Chaplin's re-edited reissue, because the reissue carries a newer score and edits.
Can I keep the music on a downloaded copy of The Kid?
Not safely. The score on many copies is Chaplin's later recording, or a modern score such as Craig Safan's 2016 work. Check what is on your copy. Replace the music or clear it before you publish.
